drivingQuestion: From where do we know that the Sages do not issue one decree to safeguard another, and how then can the prohibition of placing bird meat with cheese on one table be justified?
outcomeNote: The ḥalla proof is dismantled by Abaye and the stewpot explanation is corrected twice, ending with a decree against a primary vessel that stands; Rav Yosef's original inference is left weakened rather than formally refuted.

segments.he: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּלָא גָּזְרִינַן גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה? דִּתְנַן: חַלַּת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And from where do you say that we do not issue» one rabbinic «decree to» prevent violation of another rabbinic «decree?» The source is «as we learned» in a mishna (Ḥalla 4:8): «Ḥalla from outside of Eretz» Yisrael, which must be eaten by a priest,

segments.he: נֶאֱכֶלֶת עִם הַזָּר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, וְנִיתֶּנֶת לְכׇל כֹּהֵן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה.
segments.en: «may be eaten with a non-priest» present «at the» same «table.» The Sages did not issue a decree prohibiting this lest the non-priest partake of the ḥalla, as the separation of ḥalla outside of Eretz Yisrael is itself a rabbinic decree. This proves that the Sages do not issue one decree to prevent violation of another decree. «And» similarly, ḥalla from outside of Eretz Yisrael «may be given to any priest that» one «wishes,» even an uneducated priest who would not guard its state of ritual purity. This is in contrast to ḥalla from Eretz Yisrael, which may be given only to priests who observe the halakhot of ritual purity.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן חַלַּת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ בָּאָרֶץ, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיגְזַר מִשּׁוּם חַלַּת הָאָרֶץ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְלָא גָּזְרִינַן – אִיכָּא לְמִשְׁמָע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said to» Rav Yosef: «Granted,» your inference would be valid «if» the mishna in tractate Ḥalla had «taught us» this with regard to «ḥalla from outside of Eretz» Yisrael that had been brought «into Eretz» Yisrael. «As» in that case, «there» could be reason «to decree» against eating it while a non-priest is at the same table, despite the fact that the non-priest eating it is prohibited only by rabbinic law, «due to» the concern that one might come to eat «ḥalla from Eretz» Yisrael, which is prohibited to the non-priest «by Torah law,» at the same table as a non-priest; «and» yet «we do not decree» against this practice. If so, «there» would be grounds «to learn from» this mishna that the Sages do not issue one decree to prevent violation of another decree.

segments.he: אֶלָּא חוּצָה לְאָרֶץ, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵיכָּא לְמִיגְזַר הוּא. אֲבָל הָכָא, אִי שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ לְאַסּוֹקֵי עוֹף וּגְבִינָה, אָתֵי לְאַסּוֹקֵי בָּשָׂר וּגְבִינָה, וּמֵיכַל בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
segments.en: «But» the mishna actually teaches this halakha with regard to ḥalla from «outside of Eretz» Yisrael that remains there. It therefore proves nothing about compound decrees, as it can be claimed that the practice «is» permitted only «because there is no» reason «to decree.» Since by Torah law the obligation of ḥalla does not apply outside of Eretz Yisrael, there is no chance that such behavior will lead to transgression of Torah law. «But here, if you permit one to place» the meat of «birds and cheese» on the same table, some might «come to place» the «meat» of domesticated animals «and cheese» on a single table «and» to «eat» this «meat» cooked «in milk,» thereby transgressing a prohibition «by Torah law.»

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: סוֹף סוֹף צוֹנֵן בְּצוֹנֵן הוּא! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲלֶה בְּאִילְפָּס רוֹתֵחַ.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet objects to» the premise of Rav Yosef’s inference: Even if one were to posit that the meat of birds in milk is prohibited by Torah law, «ultimately» this is still a decree issued due to another decree, as «it is» a case of «cold» food «in» another «cold» food, consumption of which is itself prohibited by rabbinic law. «Abaye said:» It is a rabbinic «decree, lest one place» the meat with cheese «in a boiling stewpot,» which is a manner of cooking and therefore prohibited by Torah law.

segments.he: סוֹף סוֹף, כְּלִי שֵׁנִי הוּא, וּכְלִי שֵׁנִי אֵינוֹ מְבַשֵּׁל! אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲלֶה בְּאִילְפָּס רִאשׁוֹן.
segments.en: The Gemara counters: «Ultimately,» even a stewpot is only «a secondary vessel,» i.e., not the vessel that was on the fire, «and» as a rule, «a secondary vessel does not cook. Rather,» one must say that it is a rabbinic «decree, lest one place» the meat with cheese «in a stewpot» that is «a primary» vessel, i.e., that was on the fire. This is certainly cooking meat in milk, and it is prohibited by Torah law.

moves.cueHe: ומנא תימרא דלא גזרינן גזירה לגזירה?
moves.summary: demands the source for the principle Rav Yosef leaned on in the previous unit
moves.about: the source for the rule that the Sages do not issue one decree to safeguard another, on which Rav Yosef's inference rested

moves.summary: brings the mishna of ḥalla from outside Eretz Yisrael
moves.about: the mishna that ḥalla from outside Eretz Yisrael may be eaten at the same table as a non-priest and given to any priest

moves.summary: deploys that ḥalla may be eaten at a non-priest's table as proof that no decree safeguards a decree
moves.about: the ḥalla mishna is deployed to establish the premise Rav Yosef relied on, that no decree is issued to safeguard a decree

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: בשלמא אי אשמועינן
moves.summary: Abaye grants the proof only for ḥalla brought into Eretz Yisrael, which is not the case the mishna states
moves.about: whether the ḥalla mishna proves anything about compound decrees, since outside Eretz Yisrael there was no reason to decree at all, whereas permitting bird and cheese on one table could lead to animal meat and cheese

moves.cueHe: אבל הכא, אי שרית ליה לאסוקי עוף וגבינה
moves.summary: and here there is real reason to decree, since permitting bird with cheese may lead to animal meat with cheese — so Rav Yosef's inference fails

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב ששת: סוף סוף צונן בצונן הוא!
moves.summary: Rav Sheshet objects that placing them together is cold in cold, so the ban is a decree upon a decree either way
moves.about: even granting that bird in milk is Torah-forbidden, meat and cheese on one table is cold in cold, so the table ban is still a decree upon a decree

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: גזירה שמא יעלה באילפס רותח
moves.summary: answers that the decree guards against a boiling stewpot, which is cooking
moves.about: the table ban guards against one placing the meat with cheese in a boiling stewpot, which is cooking and Torah-forbidden

moves.summary: presses that a stewpot is a secondary vessel and does not cook
moves.about: a stewpot removed from the fire is only a secondary vessel, and a secondary vessel does not cook

moves.cueHe: אלא גזירה שמא יעלה באילפס ראשון
moves.summary: corrects the answer: the decree concerns a stewpot that is a primary vessel
moves.about: the decree guards against placing them in a stewpot that is a primary vessel, which does cook and so violates Torah law
